Treating prefers-reduced-motion as 'remove all feedback'. Removing every cue hurts ADHD users. Replace movement with fade or color or glyph change instead.

Not re-testing each theme: contrast, focus and target checks must run for every design x mode combination (and with prefers-contrast: more and forced-colors: active), since one theme passing says nothing about the others.
Spoken confirmation and tick sound must stay opt-in per checklist (they are). With a screen reader running, duplicate speech from speechSynthesis plus a live region is noisy (inference).
recommendations: AUTOMATABLE CHECKLIST (run per design x mode, also under prefers-contrast:more and forced-colors:active).

1. Token contrast (pure computation from CSS variables, no browser needed): composite any alpha tokens over the actual backdrop, then assert text/bg >= 4.5 for body, detail, quantity, 'required' and placeholder tokens; >= 3.0 only for tokens used at 24 px or larger (or 18.67 px bold or larger); >= 3.0 for tick-box border, check mark vs fill, focus ring vs adjacent, and divider tokens that carry meaning. No rounding.

2. Grain and gradients: for each noisy or gradient surface behind text, compute contrast against the worst-case local background (base color composited with noise at max lighter and max darker alpha; every gradient stop plus midpoint). Require >= 4.5, or require a --plate behind text.

3. Target size (Playwright): at widths 320, 360, 390 and 430, for every button, [role=button], input, a, tick row and drag-handle replacement on every screen, assert bounding box >= 24x24 as a hard fail and >= 44x44 (48 for tick rows) as the project target. Also assert 24 px circles of any undersized pair do not intersect.

4. Focus: Tab through every screen and theme. Assert computed outline-style is not none, outline-width >= 2 px (target 3 px), focus color vs adjacent >= 3:1, and focused-vs-unfocused change of contrast >= 3:1. Assert the focused element's bounding box is not fully covered (document.elementFromPoint at its corners and center resolves to it or a descendant, not the Close/Done bar).
5. Reorder: assert every draggable point has a single-tap up/down (or move-to) control and that it works by keyboard.

6. Reduced motion: emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}); assert document.getAnimations() contains no running transform, translate, scale or rotate animations and no infinite iterations; opacity and color transitions are allowed. With no-preference, motion may run.

7. Color not only: for checked/unchecked, required/optional and any status color, assert a non-color cue exists in the DOM (SVG glyph, text, shape) plus aria-checked; optionally screenshot under html{filter:grayscale(1)} and assert checked and unchecked pixels differ.

8. Forced colors: emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'}); assert the check mark is visible (screenshot diff checked vs unchecked), a focus outline renders, and grain and gradient layers are display:none or ignored.
9. High contrast: emulateMedia({contrast:'more'}); assert tokens switch to the higher-contrast set (text >= 7:1 is a reasonable policy) and grain is off.

10. Theme persistence: set the stored design and mode, reload with the opposite emulated colorScheme, and assert documentElement.dataset values are correct on first paint (init script plus a MutationObserver). Assert 'system' mode follows a live emulateMedia colorScheme change. Make localStorage throw (override Storage.prototype.getItem/setItem) and assert the app still renders a valid theme.

11. Reflow and text spacing: at 320x568, with the 1.4.12 override stylesheet injected and with root font-size scaled to 200 percent, assert no horizontal page scroll, no clipped text (scrollWidth/scrollHeight vs clientWidth/clientHeight on overflow:hidden containers), and that every action (tick, Done/Close, Save/Cancel) is reachable, via an inner scroller if needed.

12. axe-core pass (tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa, wcag22aa) per theme with zero violations; treat every color-contrast 'incomplete' as needing check 1 or 2; confirm whether the target-size rule is enabled in your axe version.
13. Status messages: assert a role=status (polite) region updates on tick and on complete, and that tick sound and speech remain off unless the checklist enables them.

DESIGN DECISIONS: (a) Ship every design with explicit light and dark token sets, or declare it single-mode with a matching color-scheme. (b) Use #121212-class surfaces and softened whites rather than #000/#FFF in dark. Keep Airplane dim, low-glare and uniform rather than glowing, and offer a red-tinted night variant only as an extra option. (c) For Modern (neobrutalism + grain), keep real 2 to 3 px borders (good for 1.4.11) and plates behind text; cap noise opacity low and disable it for prefers-contrast:more and forced-colors. (d) Settings: a 3-way Design selector (Classic / Airplane / Modern) plus a Mode selector (System / Light / Dark), plus optionally 'Motion: System / Reduce' and 'Contrast: System / High'; persist in localStorage with try/catch; default to system preferences; keep the settings controls themselves AA in every theme.

Apply the 44/48 px floor to tick rows (whole row tappable) and the right-thumb bottom-right controls; keep at least 8 px between adjacent targets; add env(safe-area-inset-bottom/right) padding so bottom-right controls are not under OS gesture areas.
Make the stack an inner scroller that only scrolls on overflow, with scroll-padding for the bottom bar, to reconcile the no-page-scroll design with Reflow, text-spacing and 2.4.11.
unverified: WebFetch could not reach any host (DNS ENOTFOUND for www.w3.org and w3c.github.io), so every W3C/MDN claim comes from WebSearch result summaries, not from reading the pages. Exact normative wording was not checked against the page text.
Exact Apple HIG (44 pt) and Material (48 dp) wording and the recommended 8 dp spacing: only secondary summaries and a W3C GitHub issue were seen, not the primary pages.
Astigmatism and halation prevalence figures (30 percent vs 50 percent) and any peer-reviewed study specifically showing white-on-black halation harm. Only design-guidance sources were found.
Any specific upper bound on contrast to avoid halation (for example capping around 15:1) has no source found; Material only gives a 15.8:1 floor.

Whether red-only night themes hurt people with protan color vision or reduce legibility on phone screens is my inference, not sourced; also the blue-light and dark-adaptation effect of a bright phone screen was not researched.

Exact Airbus/Boeing color semantics: sources were flashcards, a Spanish study document and an EASA consultation comment; AMC 25.1322, SAE ARP4102/7 and the AC 25-11A text were not read, and no night luminance numbers were found.
How background-image (url and gradient) is handled under forced-colors in each browser: one source says images are removed; I could not confirm per-browser behavior.
Whether axe's target-size rule is enabled by default and its tag set (likely wcag22aa); the min axe version for stable use.
WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text (200 percent), 2.2.2 Pause/Stop/Hide, and 2.3.1 Three Flashes details were not retrieved.
Whether non-default user-selectable themes are held to WCAG conformance in an audit (only G174's alternate-version framing was found).
Safe-area inset behavior for bottom-right anchored controls on iOS and Android gesture navigation was not researched.
Whether localStorage throwing in private or blocked-storage modes affects each target browser version: a general caution, not sourced here.
